thread:
eli: Noticed spike in us-west p4 pool around 88% mem pressure. Short queue backlog, then many requests spilled to fallback with higher latency and ~12% higher cost for the hour.

mira: Where did latency move? p95/p99?

eli: p95 text-gen-default went 85ms -> 410ms, p99 ~1.6s across a 7m window. Small bump in retransmits too.

simon: Which fallback kicked in? variant fallback or cross-region?

eli: Cross-region spill (us-west -> us-east warm) plus cpu-encoder for short queries. Both.

katie: Any hard 429 rejects reported or just pacing/slowdowns?

eli: No 429s this time. Admission controller paced; lease durations were tiny so clients poll-looped, producing many small stalls.

infra-bot: incident-detect: spike route:text-gen-default window:2026-03-17T18:12Z severity:medium

mira: So two knobs: where to send overflow (local queue vs warm region vs cpu fallback) and how to pace (lease_ms, batching timeouts). Need a default UX for new admit policy.

simon: Draft config idea: admit_policy.mode = \"spill_preference\"; spill_targets ordered list; warm_region_cap_per_min; pacing. Allow per-route/cust override.

katie: Make spill_target configurable but cap warm-region egress per-minute to control cost. Also telemetry for spill counts.

eli: Quick sketch:
```
admit_policy:
  spill_preference: [local_queue, warm_region]
  warm_region_cap_per_min: 50
  pacing: { lease_ms: 500, backoff: \"exp\" }
  soft_degrade: true
```

mira: 500ms lease is more reasonable than 200ms. 200 led to busy loops in the incident. For interactive routes maybe 500-800ms.

simon: soft_degrade flow: stream an interim chunk or small partial token with header so clients can show degraded UI instead of full fallback.

katie: Add experiment metrics: spillover_count, extra_egress_bytes, p95_delta for labels like \"soft_degrade:on\".

eli: Ops ask: allow oncall to flip a temporary reject_when_pool>95% flag to bound tail latency. It will increase 429s but protect other customers.

mira: We need a clear tradeoff table (latency tail vs 429 vs cost) for PM/Support to sign off.

simon: Rollout plan: 5% canary per-route. Track request success, p95, 429 rate, cost delta, user-facing errors. If 429s spike, revert.

ops-rotations: I'll seed a canary config (prefer warm_region with warm_region_cap_per_min=20 and lease_ms=500) and push to 5%. Adding runbook & monitoring alerts. ETA ~1h.

eli: Also emit X-Redwood-Admission: <policy-id> response header for tracing.

mira: Add synthetic load tests that mirror our length distribution to validate batching behavior with longer lease_ms.

simon: This also reduces scheduler memory pressure since we avoid deeper queues that caused OOM in scheduler.

katie: Finance note: cross-region egress + infra tax. I'll model cost at 3 volumes and sync tomorrow.

Actions:
- ops-rotations: create canary + runbook (ETA 60m)
- mira: tradeoff table + experiment metrics (ETA EOD)
- simon: implement spill_targets + debug header in admit-controller (PR)
- katie: cost model + finance sync (ETA tomorrow)

ops-rotations: deploy: canary_admit_policy/1919007777 -> 5% :ok_hand:
infra-bot: deploy complete for 5% canary

mira: I'll check p95/429 for canary slice in 20m and report back.

eli: If 429s spike, switch canary back to local_queue. Thanks everyone :thumbsup:
